Step-by-Step Audio Guided Tour: restaurant tour of Buttermilk & Bourbon - Back Bay, Boston, MA
Tour-Category: restaurant

Stop 1: The Capital Grille

Address: 900 Boylston St, Boston, MA 02115

Coordinates: 42.348689, -71.082071

Type/Specialty: Steakhouse

Specific Examples: Classic steak cuts, extensive wine list, elegant ambiance

Orientation: You are about to embark on a walking journey through Buttermilk & Bourbon - Back Bay, Boston, MA. The route spans from The Capital Grille to Stephanie's On Newbury, a mere 414 meters apart in this urban landscape. In the bustling Back Bay, a tapestry of culinary tales unfolds, from the classic American steakhouse elegance of The Capital Grille to the innovative coastal delights at Stephanie's On Newbury. Stephanie Sokolove's dream brought forth the award-winning comfort food at her restaurant, while the neighborhood's culinary diversity invites you to savor the essence of this vibrant culinary hub. In the upcoming stops, you will learn about Stephanie's merger with her sister's restaurant portfolio in 2018 at Stephanie's On Newbury and the lawsuit filed by the Restaurant Opportunities Centers United at The Capital Grille. Your first stop is The Capital Grille. Head southeast on Boylston Street; the restaurant will be on your right after passing Gloucester Street. As you approach the gleaming facade of The Capital Grille on Boylston, just outside the Hynes Convention Center, the rich aroma of dry-aged steaks mingles with the ambient hum of Boston's bustling Back Bay.

Entering The Capital Grille means immersing yourself in a slice of Boston's political and social history. In the 1990s and 2000s, this steakhouse served as a pivotal meeting place for state house lobbyists and power brokers. Important discussions and agreements unfolded over perfectly seared steaks and a wide selection of wines. But it's not just the past that makes The Capital Grille significant; its parent company, Darden Restaurants, faced a major federal class-action lawsuit in early 2012. Organized by the Restaurant Opportunities Centers (ROC) United, the lawsuit alleged racial steering and wage theft, bringing to light the challenges within the restaurant industry. As you enjoy the plush interiors and the attentive service, consider this place's connection to broader conversations about labor rights and equality. The Capital Grille is open Monday and Tuesday from 11:30 am to 9:00 pm, offering a blend of history and high-end dining. Reservations are recommended due to its popularity. The dining experience is rich in flavor and history, with prices reflecting its fine dining status at around four dollar signs.


Directions: As you exit The Capital Grille, head south on Dartmouth Street. Stroll past the boutique shops and cafes until you reach Newbury Street. Turn left onto Newbury Street and continue walking until you reach Stephanie's On Newbury on your right. Enjoy your walk and the vibrant atmosphere of Back Bay!



Stop 2: Stephanie's On Newbury

Address: 190 Newbury St, Boston, MA 02116

Coordinates: 42.351034, -71.078163

Type/Specialty: American cuisine

Specific Examples: Brunch options, outdoor seating, trendy atmosphere

Orientation: As you meander along Newbury Street, the vibrant pulse of Boston's Back Bay, you'll find yourself at the corner of Newbury and Exeter.

Stephanie's On Newbury was opened by Stephanie Sokolove in 1994, and it quickly became a pioneer in the upscale comfort food scene. This was not just any restaurant opening; it was a culinary statement that practically invented the 'comfort food + see-and-be-seen brunch patio' trend on this prestigious street. Stephanie's vision was simple yet profound: to serve sophisticated comfort food in a relaxed, inviting setting, where the warmth of family recipes could be enjoyed by all. Together with her family, she created a local landmark that combined culinary creativity with a welcoming atmosphere. In 2018, Stephanie embarked on a new chapter by merging her restaurant portfolio with that of her sister, Kathy Sidell, under Sidell Hospitality. This merger was not merely a business decision but a union of familial talent and passion for the culinary arts. It marked a significant moment in Boston's dining scene, bringing together two sisters with a shared vision and distinct expertise. Their collaboration ensured that both Stephanie's On Newbury and Kathy's ventures could thrive, offering a diverse array of dining experiences across the city. Open on Mondays and Tuesdays from 11 AM to 10 PM, the restaurant offers dishes priced between $31 and $50, featuring contemporary American comfort food that delights locals and visitors alike.
